scope: Attempted named-foreign-shareholder (>=1%) research on five NIFTY 50 constituents — InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo), Infosys, Jio Financial Services, JSW Steel, Kotak Mahindra Bank — from each company's own latest SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) shareholding-pattern filing. This batch had unusually poor primary-source reachability: four of the five companies' own investor-relations sites returned hard blocks (Infosys: infosys.com is 403 Forbidden site-wide, every URL and method tried, including the homepage itself, not just the filing path; InterGlobe Aviation: goindigo.in is 403 Forbidden site-wide; Jio Financial Services: jiofin.com is rejected at the network layer by the outbound proxy under 'organization policy' before any HTTP response, so it could not be reached at all this pass; JSW Steel: jswsteel.in itself is reachable (200) and was crawled, but no 'Shareholding Pattern' page or PDF link could be located anywhere in its investors section within budget — the site appears to have moved or JS-renders that specific page). NSE's nsearchives.nseindia.com PDF host (documented reachable for other batches) returned 403/503 on every InterGlobe Aviation and Jio Financial Services URL tried here. BSE's static PDF-attachment host (bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/...), which SPEC noted 'often opens', returned 403 on the one Kotak Mahindra Bank filing tried. Only Kotak Mahindra Bank's own site (kotak.com, 301-redirecting to kotak.bank.in) served a shareholding-pattern PDF — but that PDF is itself only the Reg. 31 Table I/II *summary* (promoter and public shareholding by category, with one aggregate 'Foreign Portfolio Investors / Foreign Institutional Investors' line), not an itemised Table III naming individual FPI holders >=1%; the filing's own last line states the itemised version is on BSE's and NSE's websites, both of which were unreachable in this pass. Net result: for all five companies, no individual foreign holder could be named and confirmed >=1% from a primary Table III filing in this pass. What this file does contain: (1) the one real, dated, primary-sourced named-holder fact available — LIC of India's 6.66% stake in Jio Financial Services received via the 2023 demerger from Reliance Industries, a historical fact, not a current-quarter filing figure; (2) the FPI/FII aggregate percentage and quarter-end date for each of the five companies, recorded as documented voids (Kotak, from its own primary filing) or reported-tier voids (the other four, from screener.in, an aggregator, per SPEC's explicit fallback instruction) rather than as fabricated named-holder claims; (3) the mandatory comparison-set entities (BlackRock, Vanguard, NBIM, GIC, Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA), none of which could be confirmed present or absent by name in this batch, recorded honestly as such rather than omitted or guessed.

claims.d: 6.66% of Jio Financial Services Ltd's equity shares were allotted to LIC of India as part of the NCLT-approved demerger of the financial-services undertaking of Reliance Industries Ltd into Reliance Strategic Investments Ltd (renamed Jio Financial Services Ltd); record date 20 July 2023, allotment/listing reported ~21-22 August 2023 — every RIL shareholder, including LIC as an existing RIL shareholder, received one JFS share per RIL share held. This is LIC's stake at listing, not a current-quarter SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) figure: Jio Financial Services' own most recent shareholding-pattern filing was not reachable in this pass (jiofin.com is rejected at the network layer by the outbound proxy; see voids), so LIC's current % is not confirmed here. screener.in's aggregate DII (domestic institutional investor) category for Jio Financial Services stood at 13.27% as of the quarter ended 30 June 2026 — a bucket LIC sits within, alongside other domestic insurers and mutual funds, so 13.27% is not LIC's number alone.

voids.what: Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd: the company's own site (kotak.com, 301-redirecting to kotak.bank.in) DID serve a primary filing — 'Shareholding Pattern as on September 30, 2025' — but that PDF contains only the Reg. 31 Table I/II summary, not an itemised Table III. From it: Promoter & Promoter Group (Individuals/HUF) 25.87% + Bodies Corporate 0.01% = 25.88% total; Mutual Funds/UTI 20.77%; Insurance Companies 9.01% (aggregate, not broken out by insurer — LIC's specific % within this is not stated); Financial Institutions/Banks 0.06%; Foreign Portfolio Investors/Foreign Institutional Investors 29.75% (59,16,42,463 of 1,98,85,92,513 shares) — the single largest public category and the one this batch cares most about, but not broken into named holders; Bodies Corporate (public) 1.83%; Resident Individuals 8.50%; Non-Resident Individuals 0.57%; Foreign Companies 0.91%; Foreign Banks 0.00% (13,072 shares); Qualified Institutional Buyer 0.11%; Others 2.40%. The filing's own foreign-ownership-limit table shows the FPI limit utilised falling from 34.97% (30 June 2024) to 30.94% (30 June 2025) to an implied ~29.75% at this quarter — a declining foreign share over five quarters. The filing states the itemised Table III is on BSE's and NSE's websites; the one BSE PDF-attachment URL located for Kotak (bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/...) returned 403.
voids.whyItMatters: Kotak Mahindra Bank is a NIFTY 50/private-bank constituent where FPI ownership (29.75%) is the largest single public category and close to the RBI's private-bank foreign-holding ceiling context; the direction of travel (falling FPI utilisation over five quarters to Sept 2025) is itself a documented, dated fact even without individual names.

symmetryCheck: This batch could not run the comparison lens at all in the sense SPEC intends: primary Table III filings (the only source that names individual holders) were reachable for zero of the five companies — Kotak Mahindra Bank's own site served a primary filing, but only the Table I/II category summary, not itemised names. So none of the eight mandatory comparison-set holders (BlackRock, Vanguard, NBIM, GIC, Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA) could be confirmed present or absent by name in any of the five. The domestic control, LIC, fares identically under the same access constraint: for four of the five companies (Infosys, InterGlobe Aviation, JSW Steel, Kotak Mahindra Bank) LIC's current holding is unknown for exactly the same reason BlackRock's is unknown — no Table III was reachable. The one point where LIC IS named (Jio Financial Services, 6.66%) is a three-year-old fact from the 2023 demerger allotment, not a current filing, and is not evidence that LIC is easier to find than a foreign holder would be — it survives only because it was independently reported by business press at the time, a channel that does not exist for routine quarterly FPI line items. In other words: this batch's finding is about source reachability (four IR sites blocked or unreachable, NSE and BSE both blocked, one company's own PDF stopping short of the named-holder table), applied identically to foreign and domestic holders alike — a symmetric failure of access, not an asymmetric pattern of disclosure or of this file's treatment of BlackRock versus LIC.

gaps: For all 5 companies in this batch, no SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) Table III (itemised public-shareholder, >=1%) data was obtained from a primary filing — the next attempt should try NSE's corporate-filings shareholding-pattern search UI directly with a real browser session (nseindia.com's API returned 404 in SPEC's own reconnaissance and in this pass; the UI itself was not tried) and BSE's stock-specific 'shareholding-pattern' listing pages (e.g. bseindia.com/stock-share-price/.../shareholding-pattern/), which were not attempted for any of these 5 beyond one blocked PDF attachment.

Infosys' FY2026 Form 20-F on SEC EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000119312526270520/infy-20260331.htm) was located but exceeded this session's fetch size limit and was not read; it likely contains a 'Major Shareholders' item with named beneficial-ownership detail and should be fetched in page ranges or downloaded directly in a follow-up pass.

jiofin.com is blocked at the network/proxy layer ('organization policy'), not merely by the target server — this is a different failure mode from the other four and may need a different route (e.g. a cached/mirrored version, or NSE/BSE direct) rather than retrying the same domain.

marketscreener.com's InterGlobe Aviation shareholder table (GIC 2.984%, Norges Bank 1.37%, several domestic AMCs) was fetched and is internally consistent, but its provenance (does it reflect SEBI Reg. 31 Table III, a different disclosure, or a blend of holdings-based-on-13F/other filings) could not be established within budget; it should be corroborated against a primary filing before being promoted from 'noted in a void' to an actual claim.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's Insurance Companies aggregate (9.01%, 30 Sept 2025) almost certainly includes LIC as the largest single line — LIC is known to be a large holder of Indian bank equity generally — but the primary source opened does not break this out by name; a Table III pull (BSE/NSE) would very likely resolve this specific figure.

Jio Financial Services' LIC stake is stale (6.66% as of the August 2023 demerger allotment); LIC's current % (likely different, given screener.in's Jun 2026 DII aggregate of 13.27% for the whole company across all domestic institutions) was not found.

This file does not cover foreign adviser mandates or the World Bank/IMF/Soros narratives — out of scope for a holders-only file, per the same exclusions the companion holders.json file already recorded for the domain as a whole.
